clue.text: Hard work, introducing a new rallying cry

parts.note: a slog is a long spell of hard work

explanation.surface: A tough job begins with a fresh call to arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto shouted to rouse supporters is a catchphrase of exactly this kind.

clue.text: Weapon provided gratis for the'. mercenary?

definitions.text: Weapon provided gratis for the'. mercenary?

parts.words: Weapon provided gratis for the'. mercenary?
parts.note: add a word meaning gratis before this spear and you get a word for a soldier of fortune

explanation.surface: A hired soldier is handed a free weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: A mercenary was a freelance: put 'free' (gratis) before the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear carried by a mounted knight is the weapon meant.

clue.text: Not : necessarily an indication that one's performance is sliding

definitions.text: Not : necessarily an indication that one's performance is sliding

parts.words: Not : necessarily an indication that one's performance is sliding
parts.note: the sliding is a musical slide up or down a scale, not a decline in quality

explanation.surface: A gentle warning that a slip in form need not mean decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliding' suggests getting worse; in music a marking can tell a player to slide between notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction for a rapid slide through a run of notes.

clue.text: Beat up one supported by the state

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them
the Roman numeral I is one
something sitting on another is supported by it

explanation.surface: A thrashing for someone backed by the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A country with its own government is a sovereign country or people.

clue.text: Unable to solve this puzzle if so stupid?

definitions.text: Unable to solve this puzzle if so stupid?

parts.words: Unable to solve this puzzle if so stupid?
parts.note: read literally, a crossword lacking its hints could not be solved; the everyday sense is dim-witted

explanation.surface: A solver too dim to finish today's crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the split reading: a puzzle without its clues is impossible, and a person without a clue is stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without any idea is colloquially being dim or ignorant.

clue.text: Poor men at UNESCO, perhaps, living at the same time

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Impoverished staff at the UN agency, all of one era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'perhaps' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: People or events of the same period are coeval.

clue.text: Unlucky direction taken by ..nurses of old

parts.note: unto is an old word for to, expressing direction
nurses work on a hospital ward

explanation.surface: An unfortunate route taken by nurses in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of old' marks UNTO as archaic; 'taken by' links the ward to the nurses who staff it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word once meant unfortunate or adverse, as of events that turn out badly.

clue.text: Look around a steamship for a rope

indicators.note: around means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Inspecting a steamer for some rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: A noosed rope for catching cattle is a cowboy's rope.

clue.text: Initially extremely radical, this Scottish writer

definitions.text: Initially extremely radical, this Scottish writer

parts.words: Initially extremely radical, this Scottish writer
parts.note: the writer's initials are R L S, which are the outer letters of radical followed by the first of Scottish

explanation.surface: A Scottish author who was very left-wing at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Louis Stevenson signed himself RLS: the first and last letters of 'radical' plus S of 'Scottish'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edinburgh author of Treasure Island and Kidnapped.

clue.text: Vague impulse to embrace a girl …

indicators.note: to embrace something is to hold it within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an instinct is an innate impulse
Di, short for Diana, is a crossword's stock girl's name

explanation.surface: A hazy urge to hug a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' marks a container: Di, a stock crossword girl, sits within the word for impulse rather than beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blurred or unclear is vague in outline.

clue.text: Outstanding player's progeny

explanation.surface: A star sportsman's children.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis player ranked in advance is seeded; offspring are also called seed, as in biblical language.

clue.text: Sound produced by parts of piano — everything depends on it

indicators.note: the sound comes from the piano parts, so those parts are written before it

parts.note: a piano's keys are the parts that are struck
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: Musing on how a piano makes its sound and what it all hinges on.
explanation.definitionFit: The central stone of an arch holds the rest in place, hence the crucial principle on which all relies.

clue.text: German shepherd, possibly, reproducing low sounds

explanation.surface: An Alsatian dog that copies deep noises.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is something that barks 'woof'; a loudspeaker for bass frequencies has the same name.

clue.text: Marshy land harbouring river plant

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, as in eastern England

explanation.surface: A bog with a stream running through it where plants grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracken-like frond-bearing plant is a classic example of the type.

clue.text: Official h.as about four put to death

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: to execute is to put to death
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An official has some four people executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is only a link here; 'about' tells you the Roman four is wrapped by the verb for executing.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior manager or administrator is an official.

clue.text: A blissful place for an animal park

explanation.surface: Somewhere heavenly to keep beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven or Eden is a place of perfect happiness; the word comes from Persian for an enclosed park, once used of a deer park.

clue.text: Risky for us to support party split by antagonism

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece comes below, so it is written after
split by means a piece is broken open and another placed in it

parts.note: a do is a party
anger is hostility or antagonism
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hazardous call for us to back a party divided by hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazardous or likely to cause harm.

clue.text: Adherent has equality with most, of 28

parts.note: par means equality, as in on a par

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: the answer at 28 across, a herbal drink

explanation.surface: A follower has parity with the majority of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a committed supporter of a cause or party.

clue.text: Urbane girl coming out, supported by one of 27?

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a girl making her entry into society
to sit on something is to be held up by it
the answer at 27 across can mean manners or demeanours, and an air is one such manner

explanation.surface: A suave debutante held up by someone at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across appears to point to sailors, but here its other sense, a person's carriage or manner, gives AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone polished and charming in manner is suave or debonair.

clue.text: Most of the office? Not at all

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter is used

parts.note: Nones is the church office said at the ninth hour

explanation.surface: A question about most of a workplace, answered with a flat no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the office' is the canonical hour, not a workplace; drop the final S of NONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, as in 'none the wiser', it means in no way.

clue.text: The end of the article

explanation.surface: The conclusion of a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or goal is one's purpose; a thing or item is another sense.

clue.text: Queensland's opening pair are not commonly attractive

indicators.note: the opening pair of a word means its first two letters are taken

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of are not

explanation.surface: Queenslanders, at first sight, are not very pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmingly old-fashioned and pleasing is the sense: picturesque.

clue.text: Lazy type involved in revolutions

explanation.surface: A layabout caught up in uprisings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutions' suggests uprisings; an idler is also a wheel or gear turning in a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer avoids work; a free-running pulley or wheel spins with a belt or train of gears.

clue.text: Chateaubriand, for one, confused Lamb with 19

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, a word meaning not at all

explanation.surface: A steak dish confused with lamb and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: Chateaubriand looks like the steak, but it is the French writer, a vicomte. 'confused' rearranges LAMB plus the letters of 19 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer Chateaubriand held a French title, making him an aristocrat.

clue.text: Protective covering for the stage

explanation.surface: A cover to guard the theatre's boards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore protects clothes; the forestage projecting in front of the curtain shares the name.

clue.text: Billy's elevation in country-and-western?

parts.note: country music was once named after rural folk called billies of the uplands, so the raised ground comes before billy in that name

explanation.surface: A singer named Billy rising in the country music charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Country-and-western was once named for upland country folk; in that old name the 'elevation' sits just before 'billy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised area of land is an elevation.

clue.text: It may record points made by twenty: directors

parts.note: a score is twenty
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: A tally of points made by a large group of executives.
explanation.definitionFit: A display at a sports ground shows the points each side has made.

clue.text: Parts of .-a machine lost by people at sea

explanation.surface: Machine parts that sailors drop overboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball races supporting a rotating shaft are machine components; people who are disoriented have lost their sense of position.

clue.text: Within it is an exceptionally nourishing decoction

indicators.note: within says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An unusually nourishing brew is contained in this.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion is a drink made by steeping or boiling herbs, a kind of decoction.
